questions.question: Q1. What is the primary communication bus protocol used between internal Electronic Control Units (ECUs) in Electric Vehicles?

explanations.a: Correct. CAN bus is the standard automotive robust differential bus protocol for inter-ECU data exchange.
explanations.b: USB is consumer peripheral interface, not real-time ECU bus.
explanations.c: BLE is short-range wireless, unfit for real-time safety critical motor control.
explanations.d: SMTP is an application layer email transmission protocol.

questions.question: Q2. In a CAN bus Denial of Service (DoS) attack, how does an attacker block legitimate ECU messages?

answers.a: By flooding the bus continuously with dominant bits (ID 0x000)
answers.b: By cutting the physical copper twisted pair wires
answers.c: By increasing the battery voltage to 800V
answers.d: By disconnecting the high-voltage interlock loop

explanations.a: Correct. Low numerical CAN IDs have higher arbitration priority, so continuous 0x000 frames starve all other nodes.
explanations.b: Cutting wires is a physical sabotage, not a bus Denial of Service attack vector.
explanations.c: Battery voltage adjustments do not govern arbitration bit priority.
explanations.d: HVIL is a physical safety circuit, not network arbitration.

questions.question: Q3. What does CAN message spoofing involve?

answers.a: Injecting forged CAN frames with valid IDs to fake sensor readings or control commands
answers.b: Encrypting all payload data with 256-bit AES keys
answers.c: Lowering the transmission baud rate from 500 kbps to 10 kbps
answers.d: Replacing motor copper windings with aluminum wire

explanations.a: Correct. Spoofing injects malicious messages pretending to originate from legitimate ECUs like BMS or VCU.
explanations.b: Encryption is a security countermeasure, not an attack.
explanations.c: Baud rate changes cause bus-off errors rather than spoofing control messages.
explanations.d: Wire material is a physical motor construction factor.

questions.question: Q4. Why are standard unencrypted CAN bus networks vulnerable to cyber attacks?

answers.a: CAN frames lack built-in sender authentication and encryption mechanisms
answers.b: CAN bus cables transmit signals faster than the speed of light
answers.c: CAN controllers refuse to process messages with even-numbered IDs
answers.d: CAN bus only operates when the vehicle is connected to Wi-Fi

explanations.a: Correct. Traditional CAN protocol broadcasts plain text frames without origin verification or payload encryption.
explanations.b: Signal propagation speed obeys electromagnetic physics.
explanations.c: CAN arbitration processes any valid 11-bit or 29-bit identifier regardless of parity.
explanations.d: CAN bus is an offline internal vehicle wired network.

questions.question: Q5. What is the main function of an automotive Intrusion Detection System (IDS)?

answers.a: To detect abnormal message frequencies, payload anomalies, and illegal CAN IDs
answers.c: To charge the battery pack faster during regen

explanations.a: Correct. IDS monitors bus traffic patterns, timing, and signatures to flag and isolate malicious network activity.
explanations.b: Horsepower is governed by motor inverter limits.
explanations.c: Regenerative charging rate is governed by motor and BMS limits.
explanations.d: Tire pressure is monitored by TPMS sensors.
